title: 3DS execution and loading improvements
changes: 3DS execution uses a cache-friendly lookup table for previously decoded CPU blocks.
Background shader preparation limits outstanding work and gives required shaders priority.
Large 3DS games read ahead during sequential loading while retaining the existing memory budget.

title: Aligned screens and a smaller C-stick
changes: Portrait DS and 3DS screens share the same horizontal center while retaining the larger lower touchscreen and native aspect ratios.
Right-side controls sit farther out to stay clear of the centered touchscreen.
The 3DS C-stick is a small nub with short visual travel and an invisible touch margin.

title: Larger lower touchscreen
changes: Expanded portrait DS and 3DS layouts give the lower touchscreen more space while keeping its original aspect ratio.
Controls stay at the outer edges and clear of the picture, with shoulder buttons above and the footer below.

title: Duo display defaults
changes: Expanded Duo-sized portrait windows use the inner display geometry by default, without requiring Screen API or installed-mode hints.
Use Duo defaults restores the device preset, neutral fold alignment, normal clearance and the current console button arrangement.
Copy layout info provides local display and layout measurements for troubleshooting without sending them automatically.

title: Installed fullscreen fold and controller fit
changes: DS and 3DS account for the Home Screen status area in fullscreen, keeping the upper picture clear of the physical fold.
The lower touchscreen retains its side controls and useful size when a bottom safe area is present.
The touch settings tab sits flush with the outer edge, with space reserved beside short controller layouts.

title: DS and 3DS console layout
changes: Expanded DS and 3DS windows put the controls in the touchscreen section. Each game screen fits its own available area while keeping its native aspect ratio.
The fold stays clear of both pictures and controls. Reported display sections locate its reserved area; Fold alignment and Fold gap in the drawer provide device-local adjustment.
Portrait stacks the screens and landscape places them side by side. Compact windows and physical controllers restore your manual view.

title: Fold alignment and expanded controls
changes: DS and 3DS align their screen boundary with reported display sections and account for the Home Screen status area when finding the display center.
Expanded screen sections use their own controller layout, keeping older phone layouts from overlapping the side controls. Controls avoid one another and the horizontal fold.
Fold alignment in the touch drawer lets you fine-tune the screen boundary with a visible guide. The adjustment stays on this device.

title: DS and 3DS screen sections
changes: Open iPhone Duo and expanded touch windows give DS and 3DS one screen per section: stacked in portrait, side by side in landscape, with controls along the outer left and right edges.

Screen sections: Auto in the touch drawer follows rotation and restores your manual view when the window becomes compact or a controller is connected. Picking a manual View turns Auto off on this device.
Native touchscreen input, screen aspect ratios and saved controller layouts are retained.

title: iPhone Duo and compact game layouts
changes: Game Boy and Game Boy Color keep their default picture clear of the controls: above them in portrait, between the side controls in landscape, with Select/Menu/Start below.
Compact portrait windows fit the default Game Boy/Color and PlayStation picture without stretching it. Fill and zoom settings remain available.
Responsive library and controller checks now cover iPhone Duo's cover display, inner display and Split View, including fold/unfold resizing. Saved controller layouts are retained.

title: Wii and Dolphin improvements available by default
changes: Nintendo Wii is included in the standard release without an enable switch or experimental labels, including browsers that disabled the beta. Existing saves and controller layouts are retained.
Wii supports ISO, single-file WBFS and Wii CISO discs, with Remote/Nunchuk layouts and optional phone motion. Its optional performance readout is in Core Settings.

GameCube and Wii gain compiled-block chaining, bounded cold-code retirement and native graphics frame skip. Desktop GameCube can use a larger cache; standard/mobile limits and save compatibility are retained.
Frame skip Off/2×/3×/4× omits native graphics work while game state and audio continue. Compatibility and speed depend on the game, browser and device.

title: PlayStation 2 available by default
changes: PlayStation 2 is available without an enable switch, including browsers that previously disabled it.
PlayStation 2 uses its standard name throughout the library and launcher. Its optional performance readout is in Core Settings.

title: PS2 and GameCube improvements
changes: Optional PlayStation 2 support is now included in the stable image. Enable it in Experimental Settings; compatibility and speed depend on the game and device.
GameCube receives rendering, disc streaming, shader caching and save-state memory improvements, including the Zelda green-screen repair.
Touch sticks preserve fine movement and full diagonal range. Connected controllers hide touch controls, with a manual toggle available.
Cloud saves recover expired sessions and handle large Nextcloud transfers more reliably. Mobile audio resumes more reliably after interruptions.

title: Mobile save-state menus
changes: Save-state previews and actions fit phone and tablet screens without clipping.
Save-slot menus size to their content with readable timestamps and accessible Load, Save and Delete controls.

title: Metadata request recovery
changes: Metadata requests stop when leaving the library, recover from temporary failures, and respect provider cooldowns.
Provider metadata refreshes when its cache expires while imported and offline details remain available.

title: Shared library scanning
changes: Shared-folder PBP games are identified as PlayStation or PSP from their format, so PSP games no longer require a PlayStation BIOS.
The shared managed folder is scanned by default with the config and ROM mounts.

title: PlayStation loading placement
changes: PlayStation loading, progress and starting messages appear in the game picture area, including before the core starts.

title: PlayStation touch controls
changes: PlayStation shows both DualShock sticks from the start, without controller pop-in when a game switches modes.
The PlayStation audio activation prompt appears over the game picture.

title: PlayStation portrait centering
changes: PlayStation uses an independent default portrait picture area above the standard controls. Controller layout changes leave picture placement unchanged; desktop stays centered.

title: PlayStation portrait layout
changes: The PlayStation game view sits near the top in portrait, keeping its native size and controller layout.

title: Simpler server storage
changes: Server deployments now use one configuration folder and one game folder. Existing game URLs, saves and settings are preserved.

title: GameCube performance readout is optional
changes: The *GameCube performance readout* now starts off by default. Enable it in Settings > Core Settings; your saved choice is preserved.

title: Mobile play and a refreshed library
changes: *PSP support*: available by default, with streaming for large games. HTTPS and WebGL2 are required.
A compact *mobile library* with search, touch controls and game details. Install as a web app for a full-screen experience.
A centered app icon, a clearer *Recently Played* history icon and distinct console artwork on mobile and desktop.
Desktop console artwork leaves the system name to the carousel, keeping category labels clear and readable.
*Recently Played restores automatically* when the library opens, including your connected account's cached and cloud history.
Installed web apps use the full display height for the library and games, with your saved touch-button positions preserved.
Installed iPhone/iPad apps request an opaque black system status bar to reduce top-edge fading. Games fill the available display and saved controls remain intact.
*Nextcloud saves* with optional automatic sign-in when enabled. Recently Played and controller layouts sync when connected.
An integrated folder scanner and feed builder, with startup scans and scheduled refreshes when enabled.
*PlayStation discs and larger 3DS ROMs stream during play* and require an internet connection.
*3DS shaders cache as they are created.* New shaders can briefly hitch, especially when many appear at once on mobile.
